invariantAllocations.invariant: ProgramKit-owned Development Tools C# satisfies the current private repository source-quality policy.
invariantAllocations.rationale: The existing private PKCS analyzer and build spine already enforce ProgramKit repository source structure and behavioral rules.

invariantAllocations.invariant: New ProgramKit projects preserve approved reference direction and exact package topology.
invariantAllocations.rationale: The existing build spine, explicit solution graph, locked restore, and architecture conformance tests own static dependency enforcement.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Consumer applications and proof fixtures consume ProgramKit only from exact locally prepared packages and controlled NuGet source mapping.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Consumer workspace topology, package provenance, source mapping, and absence of project/source/build coupling require isolated filesystem and build conformance.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Manifests, executables, provider configuration, ownership locks, MCP behavior, permissions, lifecycle, and cold-session evidence conform to their exact contracts.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Byte integrity, process behavior, provider discovery, permission observation, and cross-session isolation cannot be proven by a C# analyzer.

rationale: The existing private ProgramKit C# gate is compatible with the ProgramKit-owned implementation. Package-only consumer and runtime/provider behavior remain explicit executable conformance obligations. No new analyzer, gate extension, or consumer attachment is justified.
residualRisks: The private ProgramKit gate remains a repository-specific monolith with an MSBuild trust boundary.
Static analysis cannot prove package-only construction, exact bytes, process isolation, provider trust or permissions, cold-session discovery, or genuine external Claude Code evidence.
nonStaticClaims: Schema projection, canonical serialization, MCP initialization/list/call, byte verification, timeout, cancellation, concurrency, idempotency, provider configuration, collision, update, removal, and package-only behavior require dedicated executable tests.
Genuine Codex and Claude Code cold-session evidence and human review remain authoritative for provider discovery, trust, permission, and non-autonomous behavior.
